newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended sharply higher, rallying after latest U.S. jobs data released Friday which showed little sign of wage inflation.

The March confederate bond futures contract ended at a new high of 119.00, up 51 basis points. The level was seen as resistance for the contract, which has risen by roughly two full points since late January.

Cash yields were also nearing lows unseen since the late 1970s. The average public yield was calculated at midday at 3.62 percent before the market rallied. That was near the 1996 and 1995 lows of 3.59 and 3.58 percent, respectively.

The curve flattened. March EuroSwiss futures traded on LIFFE ended down seven basis points at 98.20. Traders said there was a liquidity shortage in Swiss short-term money one trader speculated may have been caused by demand from one large bank. The Swiss National Bank added liquidity this morning.
March Comi medium-term bond up nine at 111.59
Mar Euro Swiss francs down seven at 98.20.
